dek: MediaTek has moved Dimensity 9500 from a flagship SoC announcement into a named premium-tablet design-in: Samsung's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and S12+. The devices are scheduled to reach retail from October 7, while MediaTek's standalone chip supply terms and volumes remain private.
summary: MediaTek confirmed on September 30 that Dimensity 9500 powers Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+. Samsung's own announcement corroborates the processor choice for both models. MediaTek describes the platform as a TSMC 3 nm design with an All Big Core CPU, NPU 990 with Generative AI Engine 2.0 and a 12-core GPU. The important change is commercial rather than purely architectural: a named global OEM has adopted the flagship SoC in a premium tablet family. MediaTek says major-retailer availability begins October 7, which is still in the future as of October 5. The sources do not disclose standalone SoC pricing, MOQ, lead time, production volume, Samsung purchase quantity or the identity of other component suppliers.

whyItMatters: A named premium-tablet design-in is stronger commercial evidence than a chip launch because it ties the SoC to a specific shipping product family and OEM.

The move extends MediaTek's flagship mobile AI architecture into a larger-screen device where on-device generative AI, multitasking and sustained thermal behaviour become more visible design constraints.
For Taiwan's supply chain, the event creates a real platform to watch, but it does not by itself identify memory, storage, camera, power, PCB, thermal, ODM or EMS winners.

reporting.heading: What changed
paragraphs: Dimensity 9500 now has a confirmed Samsung tablet design-in. MediaTek says the SoC powers both Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and S12+, and Samsung's official launch material independently lists the same application processor for the two models.

MediaTek also provides the retail timing: availability at major retailers is due to start October 7. Because this article is dated October 5, that date is reported as an announced future launch rather than proof that units are already on shelves.

reporting.heading: Design and commercial implications
paragraphs: For product teams, the significance is that MediaTek's flagship mobile AI stack is being used in a premium tablet, creating another reference point for local AI, graphics and power-management trade-offs beyond smartphones. MediaTek's NPU and GPU figures remain vendor specifications rather than independent application benchmarks.

The named Samsung relationship is official, but its commercial boundaries matter. Neither company discloses SoC unit price, MOQ, lead time, purchase quantity or production allocation. The announcement also does not justify assigning other component or manufacturing work to specific suppliers without separate first-party evidence.

flypigTake: This is the kind of signal that matters more than another peak-performance slide: Dimensity 9500 has crossed into a named premium device from Samsung. The next questions are execution questions, not announcement questions: how the platform behaves under sustained tablet workloads, how broadly Samsung deploys it by market, and whether MediaTek wins more large-screen AI devices after this launch.
